Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Δεκεμβρίου, «Αγία Λουκία η παρθένος», with the rank word and «η παρθένος» left off. The page's hymns print the vocative «Λούκια» once beside «Λουκία»; the nominative of the calendar line is the form stored.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 13 decembrie — «Sfânta Muceniță Lucia, fecioara»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Αγία Λουκία η παρθένος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same woman: the virgin of Syracuse martyred under Paschasios and Diocletian. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page agrees with the folder's year, «μαρτύρησε κατά το έτος 304 μ.Χ.», so `dates` are left untouched. It adds a great deal the folder did not have: her mother Eutychia's haemorrhage and their refuge at the shrine of Agatha in Catania; the raising of a church in her honour by Leo bishop of Catania in 886; the translation of her relics to Constantinople, their removal by the crusaders in 1204 and to Venice in 1280, their keeping since 1860 in the church of Saints Jeremiah and Lucy, and the silver revetment put on her head in 1955; and the European customs of her day, in Sweden and at Palermo. The places are named but no coordinate is proposed. It prints two apolytikia and two kontakia, all four naming her, which are taken; and a megalynarion with a second megalynarion, an oikos and four kathismata with an idiomelon, which are kinds the schema does not hold.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Lucia, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un Milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Mucenițe Lucia, fecioara din Siracuza (the common of a virgin martyr, «Mielușeaua Ta, Iisuse», with her name in it)

english.text: Your lamb Lucia cries out to you with a loud voice, Jesus: you, my Bridegroom, I love; seeking you, I suffer; I am crucified and buried together with you in your baptism; I suffer for you, that I may reign in you; I die for you, that I may live for you. Receive me as an unblemished sacrifice, offering myself to you in love. By her prayers, in your mercy, save our souls.

hymns.text: Σικελίας τὸ κλέος, ᾽Εκκλησίας ἀγλάϊσμα, καὶ τῆς οἰκουμένης ἁπάσης τὸ στερρότατον ἔρεισμα, Λουκίαν ὑμνήσωμεν πιστοί, ὡς Μάρτυρα Χριστοῦ τὴν θαυμαστήν, παρθενίᾳ κοσμουμένην καὶ ἀρετῶν χαρίσμασι διαλάμπουσαν. Δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι αὐτήν, Δόξα Χριστῷ τῷ στερρώσαντι. Δόξα τῷ δωρουμένῳ τοῖς πιστοῖς στέφος τὸ ἄφθαρτον.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α', Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης, on the page of Αγία Λουκία η παρθένος. It names her.

english.text: The glory of Sicily, the adornment of the Church and the firmest stay of the whole inhabited world: let us the faithful hymn Lucia as the wonderful martyr of Christ, adorned with virginity and shining with the gifts of the virtues. Glory to him who strengthened her, glory to Christ who made her steadfast, glory to him who grants the incorruptible crown to the faithful.

hymns.text: Παρθενίας φοροῦσα χλαῖναν ὑπέρλαμπρον, παρθενικῶς ἐμνηστεύθης τῷ Ζωοδότῃ Χριστῷ, καὶ ἀγάπην γεηροὺ μνηστῆρας ἔλιπες ὅθεν ὡς δῶρα νυμφικά, προσενήνοχας αὐτῶ, τὰ ρεῖθρα τῶν σῶν αἱμάτων, Λούκια Παρθενομάρτυς, ὦ καὶ πρεσβεύεις ὑπὲρ πάντων ἠμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr — Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — printed second of the two the page gives. Its «ἀγάπην γεηροὺ μνηστῆρας» is the reading the site publishes and is copied unchanged, on the page of Αγία Λουκία η παρθένος. It names her.

english.text: Wearing the surpassingly bright mantle of virginity, thou wast betrothed as a virgin to Christ the Giver of life, and didst leave behind the love of an earthly suitor; wherefore thou hast offered him, as a bridal gift, the streams of thine own blood, O Lucia, virgin-martyr, who also intercedest for us all.

hymns.text: Χρυσοῖς κροσσωτοῖς, στολήν σου ἐποίκιλας, καὶ ταύτῃ λαμπρῶς, τῷ θρόνῳ παρίστασαι, τοῦ Δεσπότου πάνσεμνε, ἀπολαύουσα, τῶν τούτου θείων δωρεῶν, αἰτουμένη πᾶσι θείαν ἔλλαμψιν.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β', Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν, on the page of Αγία Λουκία η παρθένος. It names her.

english.text: With golden fringes thou didst embroider thy robe, and in it thou standest in splendour before the throne of the Master, O all-revered one, enjoying his divine gifts and asking divine illumination for all.

hymns.text: Τὴν λαμπράν σου ἄθλησιν, ἀνευφημοῦντες ἐν πόθῳ, ὡς ἁγνὴν παρθένον σε, καὶ ἀθληφόρον τιμῶμεν· μόνον γὰρ, Χριστοῦ τὸ κάλλος ἐπιποθοῦσα, ἅπασαν, ἀπεβδελύξω φθαρτῶν ἰδέαν· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ τμηθεῖσα, ἀφθάρτου δόξης Λουκία ἔτυχες.

source.text: saint.gr — Έτερον Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — printed second of the two the page gives, on the page of Αγία Λουκία η παρθένος. It names her.

english.text: Acclaiming thy bright contest with longing, we honour thee as a pure virgin and a bearer of the prize; for desiring the beauty of Christ alone, thou didst abhor every form of corruptible things, and therefore, being beheaded, thou didst obtain incorruptible glory, O Lucia.
